Check the 572-line diff against the factory's CODING_STANDARDS.md and the smell baseline, and sort each finding as would-break, fails-open, standards breach, or fix-alongside.
input.done: A Markdown report exists at .scratch/review/ab47eb9/standards-report.md. It has exactly four `## ` headings in the given order: Would break, Fails open, Standards breaches, Fix alongside. Items are numbered continuously across all four headings. Each item opens with a bold title and has the quoted hunk in a fenced block under it. Every Would break or Fails open item also carries a `Documented step:` line and a `Result:` line. The report stays under 400 words and ends with exactly one line `hard findings: N`, counting only the first two sections. My reply is only that path. Zero findings is an acceptable result.
input.may_change: I can read the diff file, and I can read single functions or sections of the code around a hunk when a finding needs that. I can create the one report file.
input.must_not: I must not run any command: no tests, no build_knowledge, no git. I must not read whole files or anything beyond what the brief allows, which also rules out the repo's usual onboarding reading. I must not edit the code under review, generated files, or vendored files. I must not count smells or inputs that are refused with a clear correction message as hard findings. I must not reply with anything other than the path.

Whether the 400-word limit includes the quoted hunks inside fenced blocks.
Whether the report needs the model and harness footer that comments posted to PRs carry. The report isn't posted, so I would leave it off.
Whether .scratch/review/ab47eb9/ already exists. Creating the file would create the directory if it doesn't.
